accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England Year 4 number and place value statement 'order and compare numbers beyond 1000' and CCSS 4.NBT.2 (compare multi-digit numbers with >, =, <). Every comparison recomputed by place: 1,999 < 2,001 (Th 1 < 2); 4,321 > 4,312 (T 2 > 1); 6,050 > 6,005 (T 5 > 0); 8,016 < 8,106 (H 0 < 1); 987 < 1,203 and 995 < 2,050 (0 thousands); order 1,876 < 4,312 < 4,321 < 9,045; cards 3,0,7,5 give 7,530 and 3,057; 4,□52 > 4,751 holds for 7, 8, 9 only (4,752 wins on the ones). All item answers checked at range corners by the items gate.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented multi-digit comparison errors (NCETM Year 4 place value guidance; Resnick et al. on decimal/whole-number comparison rules): comparing from the ones, adding the digits, 'more 9s is bigger', aligning numbers by their first digit (987 vs 1,203), a leading zero when making the smallest number, reversing < and >, and treating a tie in the hundreds as equality (the 7 case in 4,□52). Each has its own message in pickSign, slide, putDigit, tryGap or the challenge.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed under 30% against all flagship labs, including flag_cmp2d.js (two-digit compare), flag_10k.js (placing on a 0–10,000 line) and flag_pvc.js (digit values). No other lab slides a shorter number into its place value columns, builds the biggest and smallest 4-digit numbers from cards with a zero, or hunts every missing digit that keeps an inequality true.

lab_teaches.evidence: Six steps: decide four pairs and see the deciding column light up, slide 987 and 995 until ones sit under ones and a grey 0 appears in the thousands, order four numbers with two that tie to the tens, build 7,530 then 3,057 from cards, find 7, 8 and 9 for 4,□52 > 4,751, then the challenge. The learner acts first; the banner states the rule only after each task is done.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 1,999 vs 2,001 ('it has more 9s'), the smallest number from 3, 0, 7, 5 (0,357 is tempting), and whether 7 can fill 4,□52 > 4,751 (many say it must be more than 7). The reveal names the learner's own choice after the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions (sign for 5,067 and 5,607, largest of 6,102/5,999/998, ordering 2,089/2,098/2,809, smallest from 0,4,1,9, digit for 4,6□0 < 4,630, 987 vs 1,203) with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: ones first, same digits different places, more nines, length-blind, backwards list, leading zero, tens/ones swap, equality is not less than, bigger tens, left-aligned columns, adding digits.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons readability passed: kid text grade about 1.3 and adult about 3.5 on learn/readability.py, well inside 6.5 and 9.5. Kid paragraphs use short sentences and concrete numbers; less than and greater than are defined where the signs first appear. Canvas banners are one or two short sentences that wrap inside the card at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler patterns and the explanation is under 12% shingle overlap with 610 (place value of each digit), 616 (two-digit compare) and 881 (numbers to 10,000). Each kid paragraph does one job: compare by columns, fewer digits and many nines, ordering and the signs, digit cards with a zero.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 × 640 (2x) in light and dark for all six steps: the Th/H/T/O grid fits four 64 px cells, sign chips and digit cards are at least 44 px tall, the order slots show four 4-digit numbers without clipping, and the missing-digit pad wraps to two rows of five. The final line-up state was fixed after the first sheet showed 995 misaligned once both pairs were done.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap or drag has a button twin (<, =, > with spoken names, Slide left/right, one button per number to order, Card 3/0/7/5 plus Clear, Try 0–9). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the pair, the column positions, the order so far, the slots or the digits found. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations, and the wrong-path click sweep raised no console errors.
